quiz.e: “He has established the world by his wisdom.” (Jeremiah 10:12)

units.title: The Vast Starry Sky
units.sub: From the earth to the edge of the observable universe, step by step we measure the heavens made by God's hand.

share.v: Lift up your eyes on high, and see who has created these, who brings out their army by number. He calls them all by name.

blocks.h: Light can circle the earth seven and a half times in one second. Yet light from the farthest reaches of the universe has traveled for more than ten billion years to reach our eyes.

Lift up your eyes on high, and see who has created these, who brings out their army by number. He calls them all by name. By the greatness of his might, and because he is strong in power, not one is lacking.
A patch of sky the size of a grain of sand

In 1995, the Hubble Space Telescope pointed at a tiny, seemingly empty patch of sky near the Big Dipper and photographed it continuously for ten days. That patch was only about one 24-millionth of the whole sky, like a grain of sand held at arm's length. Yet about three thousand galaxies appeared in the picture.
If each galaxy were a city, that sand-grain-sized patch of sky would be packed with three thousand cities, and each city would be home to a hundred billion stars or more.
How many galaxies are there?

Our own Milky Way is about 100,000 light-years across and holds 100 to 400 billion stars. The number of galaxies in the observable universe is estimated at somewhere between several hundred billion and more than a trillion.

The observable universe is about 93 billion light-years across. That is larger than “the age of the universe × the speed of light,” because space itself has been expanding while the light was on its way.

A 2016 study estimated that there may be as many as two trillion galaxies; in 2021, New Horizons measured the cosmic background light from beyond Pluto and arrived at a much lower estimate, about several hundred billion. This is science's ongoing process of correction at work.
The Hubble Deep Field image captured about three thousand galaxies in a tiny region of sky.
Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach the earth; the nearest star, Proxima Centauri, is about 4.24 light-years away; the Andromeda Galaxy is about 2.5 million light-years away.
The number of galaxies in the observable universe is roughly several hundred billion to more than a trillion; estimates from different methods still differ widely.

The vastness of the universe does not mean human beings are unimportant; on the contrary, the Bible says the God who made all the host of heaven cares especially for people. This is a declaration of faith, and the heart of this unit.
His eternal power: the God who counts the stars
He counts the number of the stars. He calls them all by their names.
Humanity, with its best telescopes, still cannot count how many galaxies there are; yet God can call every star by name. However big the universe is, his power is bigger still.

Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and marked off the sky with his span, and calculated the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance?
What comes next in the same passage

Why do you say, Jacob, and speak, Israel, “My way is hidden from Yahweh, and the justice due me is disregarded by my God”? … He gives power to the weak. He increases the strength of him who has no might.
Right after Isaiah speaks of the vast starry sky, he turns to people who are weary. The God who counts the stars also counts your tears.
Look up at the sky tonight and try counting how many stars you can see. Then remember: he can call every one of them by name, and he can call you by name too.
Reflect: How big are my troubles when set within the universe? And how big are they before God?

Prayer: Lord, you mark off the heavens with the span of your hand, and my burden is not heavy in your hands. Please give strength to me in my weariness, and let me mount up with wings like an eagle. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Focus on Jesus: not on myself, not on others, not on my circumstances. I look to the Lord who is greater than the universe.
From an earthly perspective to a heavenly one: the problem hasn't gotten smaller, but I see that God is bigger.
Humility overcomes pride: under the vast starry sky, no one can go on thinking they are great.

blocks.h: This week: find a friend who is going through a weary season, send them Isaiah 40:26–31, and pray for them.
Quiz

quiz.q: About how many galaxies did the Hubble Deep Field capture in a tiny patch of sky?
quiz.e: About three thousand galaxies, and that patch of sky was like a grain of sand seen at arm's length.

quiz.q: About how long does sunlight take to travel from the sun to the earth?
quiz.e: About 8 minutes 20 seconds; light from Proxima Centauri takes 4.24 years.

quiz.q: After describing the starry sky, whom does Isaiah 40 go on to comfort?
o: People who are weary and weak
quiz.e: “He gives power to the weak. He increases the strength of him who has no might.” (Isaiah 40:29)

units.title: Let There Be Light
units.sub: The first words of creation were “Let there be light.” The mysteries of light still amaze physicists today.

share.v: God is light, and in him is no darkness at all.

blocks.h: Every color you are seeing right now is light. Yet the light the human eye can see is only a very narrow slice of the whole electromagnetic spectrum.

Even more wonderful: the band where the sun gives off the most energy, the band where the atmosphere is most transparent, the band where water is most transparent, and the band our eyes can see almost all overlap in the same narrow window.
God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.
The universe's speed limit
The speed of light in a vacuum is 299,792,458 meters per second. This value never changes, and since 1983 it has been used directly to define how long “one meter” is.
Light is like the universe's messenger. Because the messenger takes time to travel, every star we see is showing us “how it used to look”: the farther we look, the older the universe we see.
A just-right window

Visible light has wavelengths of roughly 380 to 750 nanometers. The peak of the sun's radiation falls right here; earth's atmosphere is almost transparent in this band while absorbing much of the harmful ultraviolet and some of the infrared; and water is transparent only in this band, which lets life in the oceans carry out photosynthesis.

The energy range photosynthesis needs, and the energy range needed by the light-sensitive molecules in our eyes, also fall within the same window. Biochemist Michael Denton calls this a chain of astonishing “coincidences.”

Each of these phenomena has a physical explanation; for example, the energies at which molecules absorb light naturally fall in this range. But the question is: why do the laws of nature happen to make so many conditions favorable to life at the same time?
The speed of light in a vacuum is 299,792,458 meters per second, a constant defined by the International System of Units.
The farther we look, the earlier the universe we see: light from the Andromeda Galaxy has been traveling for about 2.5 million years.
Earth's atmosphere and liquid water are both fairly transparent in the visible band and strongly absorbing in many other bands.
That so many favorable conditions fall within the same narrow window points to purposeful design. This is a philosophical inference, and scholars differ on what it means.
God is light, and in him is no darkness at all.
His divine nature: goodness and holiness
Light makes all things visible, and it lets life grow. God placed light on the first day of creation, as if to say: I am giving you a world you can see and live in. This is his goodness.
In him was life, and the life was the light of men. The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn't overcome it.
I am the light of the world. He who follows me will not walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.
seeing it is God who said, “Light will shine out of darkness,” who has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
Paul connects the first light of Genesis with the moment a person comes to faith. In the beginning God lit up the universe; today he lights up the human heart.
Tomorrow morning, watch the first sunlight come into your room. That light left the sun a little over eight minutes earlier and traveled all that way for you.
Reflect: Is there a corner of my heart where I still don't want to let the light in?
Prayer: Lord Jesus, you are the light of the world. Please shine into the darkness in my heart, and make me a light for others. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: The Holy Spirit is my guide: light does not shine on everything to show off, but so people can see the path clearly. I ask the Holy Spirit to light up my next step.
Live out the life of Christ: “You are the light of the world.” Let people see my good works and glorify my Father in heaven (Matthew 5:14–16).
Selflessness: light does not shine for itself; it lights up others.

blocks.h: This week: do one good deed without expecting anything back, and let someone's life be a little brighter because of you.
Quiz

quiz.q: Why do we say “the farther we look, the earlier the universe we see”?
o: Because light takes time to travel
quiz.e: Light from far away takes a long time to arrive, so we see things as they were when the light set out.

quiz.q: Which of the following also falls within the narrow window of visible light?
o: The bands where water and the atmosphere are most transparent
The band used by cell phone signals
quiz.e: The peak of solar radiation and the transparency windows of the atmosphere and water all overlap with visible light.

quiz.q: Which verse says “God is light, and in him is no darkness at all”?
quiz.e: 1 John 1:5.

units.title: The Furnace of the Stars
units.sub: The carbon, oxygen and iron in our bodies were all forged inside stars.

share.v: when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?

blocks.h: The iron in your blood, the calcium in your bones, the carbon in every cell: none of it was made on earth. It was forged in the cores of ancient stars at temperatures of many millions of degrees.
God formed man from “the dust of the ground,” and that dust, it turns out, was fired in the furnaces of the stars.
Yahweh God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
Where do the elements come from?

items: Hydrogen, helium (and a little lithium): formed in the first few minutes after the beginning of the universe.
Carbon, oxygen, nitrogen, up to iron: in the cores of stars, lighter nuclei fuse into heavier ones.
Elements heavier than iron (such as gold and iodine): produced in supernova explosions and neutron star collisions.

blocks.h: In 1957, Margaret and Geoffrey Burbidge, William Fowler and Fred Hoyle published a classic paper that fully explained how stars make the elements. In 2017, astronomers for the first time observed a collision of two neutron stars with both gravitational waves and light, and watched heavy elements being formed.
The miracle of carbon

To form carbon, three helium nuclei must collide almost at the same moment, which should be extremely difficult. In 1953, Hoyle reasoned that the carbon nucleus must have a state at a specific energy (about 7.65 million electron volts) for carbon to be produced in large amounts. Laboratory experiments soon found exactly that state, now called the “Hoyle state.”

Hoyle himself did not believe in God, yet in 1981 he wrote that a common-sense interpretation of the facts suggests that a superintellect has “monkeyed” with physics, as well as with chemistry and biology.

Later studies have shown that the yields of carbon and oxygen are quite sensitive to the energy of the Hoyle state and the strength of the nuclear force, though precise estimates of that sensitivity are still debated.
Most elements heavier than helium were formed inside stars and in stellar explosions.
Neutron star collisions produce heavy elements such as gold; this was observed directly in 2017.
The carbon nucleus has the excited state Hoyle predicted, which allows stars to produce carbon efficiently.
The yields of carbon and oxygen are sensitive to slight changes in the nuclear force; the degree of sensitivity is still being studied.
His wisdom: a gift long in the making

Before human beings appeared, stars had burned and exploded generation after generation, preparing the materials for life. God is never in a hurry; what he prepares for us is earlier and more thorough than we can imagine.
For he knows how we are made. He remembers that we are dust.
There is one glory of the sun, another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for one star differs from another star in glory.
Paul uses the differing glory of the stars to explain the glory of the resurrection body. We who came from dust will, through Christ, one day receive glorious, imperishable bodies.
Put your hand on your chest and feel your heartbeat. Every atom in this body has gone through God's long and careful preparation.
Reflect: I am dust, yet I carry God's breath; I am small, yet I am treasured by God.
Prayer: Father, thank you that long before I was born, you were already preparing for me. My life is your gift, and I want to offer it back to you for your use. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Humility: I am dust; I have nothing to boast about.
Dignity: I carry God's breath and am made in God's image; I don't need to feel worthless.
Life first, then relationships, then ministry: God spent ages preparing the materials of life; I too will patiently let God shape my life.

blocks.h: This week: say to a friend who often feels inferior, “You are a work God carefully prepared.”
Quiz

quiz.q: Where was most of the carbon in our bodies formed?
o: In the depths of the ocean
quiz.e: Carbon is formed in the cores of stars by the fusion of helium nuclei.

quiz.q: The “Hoyle state” is connected with the formation of which element?
quiz.e: This energy state of the carbon nucleus allows stars to produce carbon in large amounts.

quiz.q: What event did astronomers observe in 2017 that confirmed the formation of heavy elements?
o: A collision of two neutron stars
quiz.e: The neutron star collision was observed with both gravitational waves and light.

units.title: A Place to See the Universe
units.sub: Earth is not only fit to live on; it also happens to be an excellent place to observe the universe.

share.v: that they should seek the Lord, if perhaps they might reach out for him and find him, though he is not far from each one of us.

blocks.h: The sun's diameter is about 400 times the moon's, and the sun is also about 400 times farther from the earth than the moon is. So, seen from earth, the moon can cover the sun exactly, without covering too much.
This means that during a total solar eclipse, scientists can see the corona around the sun, and can even see stars next to the sun in the daytime.
God said, “Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs to mark seasons, days, and years;
A total eclipse confirmed relativity

In 1919, British astronomer Arthur Eddington and his colleagues used a total solar eclipse to photograph stars near the sun, and found that starlight passing the sun was bent by an amount that matched the prediction of Einstein's general relativity. This observation made relativity world-famous.

The moon moves about 3.8 centimeters farther from the earth each year. In the distant past the moon was closer, and in the far future it will be farther away, and then there will be no more perfect total eclipses. Human beings happen to live in the era when perfect total eclipses can be seen.
A good location in the Milky Way

The solar system lies between the Milky Way's spiral arms: not in a crowded, dangerous place like the galactic core, nor at the edge where heavy elements are scarce. Astronomers call such a region the “galactic habitable zone.”

This location also gives us a clear view, less obscured by dust, of distant galaxies and the cosmic background radiation. Astronomer Guillermo Gonzalez and philosopher Jay Richards argue that the places best suited for life also happen to be best suited for observation, and that this does not look like coincidence.

Critics see this as a “selection effect”: observers able to think about these questions could only ever appear in suitable places. Supporters reply that a selection effect can explain habitability but does not necessarily explain why the same place is also suited for observation.
The sun's diameter is about 400 times the moon's, and its distance is also about 400 times greater, so during a total eclipse the two appear nearly the same size.
During the 1919 total eclipse, starlight was observed to be bent by the sun's gravity, supporting general relativity.
The moon moves about 3.8 centimeters farther from the earth each year (by laser ranging).
The Milky Way contains a “galactic habitable zone” better suited to complex life; its extent is still debated.
“Habitability and observability are correlated” is a disputed philosophical argument.

He made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the surface of the earth, having determined appointed seasons and the boundaries of their dwellings, that they should seek the Lord, if perhaps they might reach out for him and find him, though he is not far from each one of us.
His goodness: an open window
God did not only give people a home; he also gave them a window, so they could look out on the universe and understand his works. He wants to be found.
The heavens declare the glory of God. The expanse shows his handiwork. Day after day they pour out speech, and night after night they display knowledge.

Paul said this in Athens to philosophers who did not know God. He began with the created world they were familiar with and ended with Jesus rising from the dead (Acts 17:31). That is exactly the path this app follows.
The place where you live and the era you were born into are all part of God's arrangement. He put you here so that you would seek him.
Reflect: What window has God opened in my life to let me see him?
Prayer: Lord, you are not far from me. Thank you for determining my times and my boundaries. Help me seek you and glorify you right where I am. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Build God's kingdom system: God has placed me in my family, my workplace and my city, and those places are territory of his kingdom.
Let Jesus reign: my boundaries are not an accident but his arrangement; within them I obey him.
Relationships matter more than things: God lets people “reach out for him and find him,” and I want to become a window through which others come to know God.

blocks.h: This week: look up the next solar or lunar eclipse visible where you live, and invite a friend to watch it with you.
Quiz

quiz.q: Why can the moon, seen from earth, cover the sun exactly?
o: The sun's diameter and distance are both about 400 times the moon's
The moon is bigger than the sun
quiz.e: The two factors of about 400 cancel out, so the two look the same size.

quiz.q: Which theory did the 1919 total eclipse observations support?
quiz.e: Starlight was bent by the sun's gravity, as Einstein predicted.

quiz.q: According to Acts 17, why does God determine people's times and boundaries?
o: So that people would seek God
So that people would be afraid
So that people would compare themselves with one another
quiz.e: “that they should seek the Lord… though he is not far from each one of us.”

units.title: The Ordinances of Heaven and Earth
units.sub: The same laws govern everything from the earth to the ends of the universe. Science is possible because the universe is orderly.

share.v: It is because of Yahweh's loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his compassion doesn't fail. They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.

blocks.h: In 1846, before any astronomer had seen Neptune, they worked out its position with pen and paper. When the telescope was pointed in that direction, there Neptune was.

In 2015, scientists detected gravitational waves given off by the merger of two black holes more than a billion years ago, waves predicted by Einstein's equations back in 1916. The universe keeps its rules, and keeps them astonishingly well.
While the earth remains, seed time and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night will not cease.
The same laws everywhere

Analyzing the spectra of distant galaxies, astronomers find that atoms there absorb and emit light exactly as they do in laboratories on earth. The laws of physics billions of light-years away are the same as the laws here.
It is like a dictionary: whether you open it in Taipei or in London, every word means the same thing. Every corner of the universe uses the same “dictionary of laws.”
Why does mathematics work?

In 1960, Nobel laureate in physics Eugene Wigner wrote a famous essay describing the effectiveness of mathematics in the natural sciences as “unreasonable”: mathematics worked out by people on paper somehow describes the motions of distant heavenly bodies with precision.

The pioneers of modern science, such as Kepler and Newton, believed the universe was made by a rational God, and was therefore worth studying and able to be understood. To them, studying nature meant thinking the Creator's thoughts after him.

Whether the physical constants have changed very slightly over the history of the universe is still a research question. Current observations restrict any possible change in the fine-structure constant to a very small range, and there is as yet no accepted evidence of change.
Neptune was discovered in 1846 at the position predicted by mathematics.
Gravitational waves were first detected directly in 2015, in agreement with the predictions of general relativity.
The spectra of distant objects show that the physical constants are extremely uniform across the universe; whether there are extremely small changes is still being studied.
The best explanation for the order and intelligibility of the universe is a rational and faithful Creator. This is a philosophical inference.
His divine nature: faithfulness

Yahweh, who gives the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, who stirs up the sea, so that its waves roar; Yahweh of Armies is his name, says: “If these ordinances depart from before me,” says Yahweh, “then the offspring of Israel also will cease from being a nation before me forever.”

God uses the laws of the universe as a guarantee of his promises: as long as the sun and moon keep to their ordinances, his covenant with his people will not fail. Every sunrise speaks of God's faithfulness.
His Son is the radiance of his glory, the very image of his substance, and upholding all things by the word of his power.
What scientists call the “laws of nature,” the Bible calls Jesus' “word of his power.” The universe is not a machine that runs by itself; it is upheld by Christ at every moment.
Tomorrow morning when you see the sunrise, say to God, “Great is your faithfulness!”
Reflect: God never breaks faith in the universe; how could his promises to me fail?
Prayer: Faithful Lord, you uphold all things, and you uphold me. Just as the sun and moon keep your ordinances, I want to follow you faithfully every day. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: The Bible is my standard: the universe has its ordinances, and my life also needs God's word as its ordinance.
The eight steps of changing our mindset: information, revelation, conviction, practice, review, correction, repetition, multiplication. Practice them regularly, and your life will change.
Faithfulness: keep your word as God does, do what you say, and become someone others can rely on.

blocks.h: This week: set a fixed daily time for devotions, and keep it for seven days in a row.
Quiz

quiz.q: How was Neptune discovered?
o: Its position was calculated mathematically first, then it was observed
A spacecraft photographed it by chance
Ancient people saw it with the naked eye
quiz.e: It was discovered in 1846 at the position predicted by mathematics.

quiz.q: How did Wigner describe the effectiveness of mathematics in the natural sciences?
quiz.e: It is astonishing that human mathematics can describe the universe so precisely.

quiz.q: According to Hebrews 1:3, what upholds all things?
quiz.e: “upholding all things by the word of his power.”

units.title: New Heavens and a New Earth
units.sub: The universe had a beginning and is heading toward an end. But the Bible's story does not stop at heat death; it ends in renewal.

share.v: But, according to his promise, we look for new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells.

blocks.h: In 1998, two teams of astronomers observing distant supernovae found that the universe's expansion is not slowing down but actually speeding up. Three scientists received the 2011 Nobel Prize in Physics for this.
According to our current understanding, the universe will grow ever colder and darker. The stars will go out one by one, until only cold and silence remain. This is called “heat death.”
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
Everything is “wearing out”

The second law of thermodynamics says that the usable energy in a closed system keeps decreasing, and disorder (entropy) only ever increases. Hot water cools, a room left alone gets messy, and stars eventually use up their fuel.
In about 5 billion years, our sun will swell into a red giant. In the far more distant future, stars in the universe will gradually stop forming and finally go dark.
The universe is like a wound-up clock that has been ticking since the beginning, its spring slowly unwinding. That tells us two things: it was once wound up, and it will not keep running forever.

The ultimate fate of the universe depends on the nature of dark energy. Most models predict endless expansion and gradual cooling; some models discuss other possibilities. All of these are projections based on the laws we know, and they are still being studied.
The universe's expansion is accelerating (1998 supernova observations; 2011 Nobel Prize).
In about 5 billion years the sun will leave the main sequence and swell into a red giant.
The long-term fate of the universe is most likely continued expansion and gradual cooling, a “heat death,” but this depends on the nature of dark energy.
The universe itself cannot offer eternal hope; hope must come from outside the universe. This is a declaration of faith.
They will perish, but you will endure. Yes, all of them will wear out like a garment. You will change them like a cloak, and they will be changed. But you are the same. Your years will have no end.
The groaning of creation

that the creation itself also will be delivered from the bondage of decay into the liberty of the glory of the children of God. For we know that the whole creation groans and travails in pain together until now.
His eternity and righteousness: making all things new
But, according to his promise, we look for new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells.

He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain, any more. The first things have passed away. He who sits on the throne said, “Behold, I am making all things new.”
The Lord who gave the universe its beginning will also give it a new beginning. The resurrection of Jesus is the first light of dawn of the new creation.
What in your life is “wearing out”? Your health, your relationships, your dreams? Bring them before the Lord who is “making all things new.”
Reflect: Am I living for a heaven and earth that will pass away, or for a kingdom that will last forever?
Prayer: Eternal Lord, your years have no end. Turn my eyes from the temporary to the eternal. May your kingdom come, and your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. In Jesus' name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: From a temporary perspective to an eternal one: measure today's gains and losses with the ruler of eternity.
Become an overcomer: “He who overcomes, I will give to him to sit down with me on my throne.” (Revelation 3:21)
Welcome the Lord's return: build God's kingdom system, prepare for the new heavens and new earth, and let God's kingdom come in my family and my workplace.

blocks.h: This week: write down one thing you will do “for eternity,” and start on it this week.

Congratulations on completing the Cosmos Hall! From “In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth” to “I am making all things new,” you have seen the story of the whole universe, and you have seen the hero of the story: Jesus Christ.
Quiz

quiz.q: In 1998, astronomers discovered that the universe's expansion is…?
quiz.e: Observations of distant supernovae showed that the expansion is speeding up.

quiz.q: What does the second law of thermodynamics tell us?
quiz.e: Disorder only increases; the universe is wearing out like a garment.

quiz.q: What ending does the Bible give to the story of the universe?
o: New heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells
quiz.e: “Behold, I am making all things new.” (Revelation 21:5)

units.title: Black Holes: Not Even Light Can Escape
units.sub: There really is a line in the universe that you can cross but never come back from, and there is no warning sign on it.

share.v: He brought me up also out of a horrible pit, out of the miry clay. He set my feet on a rock, and gave me a firm place to stand.

blocks.h: Squeeze the whole Earth into a marble and it would be about 1.8 centimeters across. If you could really compress it that far, the Earth would become a black hole, and not even light could get out.

In late 1915, with artillery thundering on the Russian front, a 42-year-old German artillery lieutenant solved Einstein’s equations in the middle of his unit and mailed the result to Einstein. The next May he died of illness. The strange radius he calculated later became the most famous boundary in the universe.
Out of the depths I have cried to you, LORD.
From a strange solution on paper to a photograph in the sky

The solution Karl Schwarzschild published in 1916 showed that if mass is squeezed inside a certain radius, that region becomes one that light cannot leave. For a long time this was treated as a mathematical oddity; even in 1939 Einstein tried to argue that real stars would not collapse that far. In the same year Oppenheimer and Snyder calculated that a star really could collapse all the way. In 1965 Roger Penrose proved that, according to general relativity, the formation of a singularity in collapse is a robust conclusion, and he received the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics for it.

The evidence piled up step by step. Cygnus X-1, an X-ray source discovered in 1964, was identified in 1972 by two independent teams as having an unseen, heavy companion, measured in 2021 at about 21 solar masses (a 2025 study estimates it lighter, around 14 to 15, and the figure is still debated). On September 14, 2015, LIGO directly detected gravitational waves for the first time, from two black holes merging more than a billion light-years away, as energy equal to about 3 solar masses turned into ripples in spacetime. In 2019 the Event Horizon Telescope released its image of the center of the galaxy M87, whose black hole is about 6.5 billion times the mass of the Sun; in 2022 it released Sagittarius A* at the center of our own Milky Way, about 4 million solar masses.

Imagine paddling a canoe downstream toward a great waterfall. The closer you get, the faster the current. Somewhere on the river there is an unmarked line: past it, the current is faster than the fastest you can paddle. You can still turn around, you can still paddle back with all your might, and the water looks much the same as before, but every stroke only delays your arrival at the edge. The event horizon is the cosmic version of this line, except that what is flowing is space itself, and there the speed of the flow equals the speed of light.
No sign on the line

According to general relativity, a person falling into a supermassive black hole would not see or feel anything special at the moment of crossing the event horizon. The tidal forces that stretch a person like noodles become deadly only farther in; with a small black hole, a person would be torn apart even outside the horizon. Stranger still, the singularity inside the horizon is no longer a place ahead of you but more like a moment in your future. You cannot steer around it, just as you cannot steer around next Tuesday. Of course, the singularity very likely marks the point where current theory breaks down, and what really happens will have to wait for quantum gravity.

There is also a common misunderstanding: a black hole is not a cosmic vacuum cleaner. If the Sun were replaced by a black hole of the same mass, the Earth would keep orbiting in the dark and cold, its orbit unchanged. You can only be trapped if you get close enough.
Hawking radiation: beautiful, but not yet seen

In 1974 Stephen Hawking proposed that once quantum effects are included, a black hole emits extremely faint radiation and may eventually evaporate. This is a theoretical prediction that has never been directly observed: the Hawking temperature of a stellar-mass black hole is far below the 2.7 K of the cosmic background radiation, so the signal is completely drowned out. Laboratory “analog black holes,” made with sound waves in ultracold atoms, have produced related results, but those are simulations and do not equal real black holes. Whether the information that falls in is actually lost is also still debated among physicists.

In 2025 the LIGO signal GW250114 reached a signal-to-noise ratio of about 80, which allowed a cleaner test than ever before of the area theorem Hawking proposed in 1971: when two black holes merge, the total horizon area can only grow, never shrink. The result agreed with the theory.
Black holes are easily talked about as more mysterious than they are. Let us separate what is certain, what is conjecture, and what is faith.
Black holes really exist: there are three independent lines of evidence, namely dynamical measurements of X-ray binaries, LIGO’s gravitational waves, and the Event Horizon Telescope images.
General relativity predicts that nothing inside an event horizon can send a signal back to the outside; all observations so far agree with this.
The area theorem, that the total area does not decrease when black holes merge, has high-confidence observational support; but this is a test on particular events, and the testing continues.
Hawking radiation is a theoretical prediction and has not been directly observed; the true nature of the singularity and the information paradox are both unresolved.

A black hole can serve as a picture of “people cannot get themselves out by their own effort,” helping us meditate on salvation. This is an analogy, a theological application, and not a physical conclusion. The Bible does not mention black holes, and a black hole is not hell; it is a celestial object God made, and in itself it has no good or evil.
Gravity takes no bribes

Gravity treats saints and sinners alike. It does not look at status and it does not accept bribes. The Bible says God’s justice is just as real: sin has real consequences, and they do not vanish because we are in a good mood. Paul describes exactly such a person, one who wants to paddle upward and finds he has no strength.
What a wretched man I am! Who will deliver me out of the body of this death? I thank God through Jesus Christ, our Lord!

He does not say, “I will try harder.” He asks, “Who will deliver me?” The answer comes from outside. Christ Himself walked into death, the place humanity agrees is the one from which no one turns back, and on the third day came out of it again. Justice was not canceled; it was borne by Him personally on the cross, and grace was not discounted either.
Because Christ also suffered for sins once, the righteous for the unrighteous, that he might bring you to God, being put to death in the flesh, but made alive in the Spirit,
whom God raised up, having freed him from the agony of death, because it was not possible that he should be held by it.

Physically, nothing can come out from inside the horizon; there the analogy reaches its end. The gospel we proclaim begins exactly at that end: the One who made gravity is not held captive by anything He has made.
even the darkness doesn’t hide from you, but the night shines as the day. The darkness is like light to you.

Tonight, after you turn off the lights, sit in the dark for one minute. Think of that place at the center of the Milky Way from which not even light escapes. It too is before God’s eyes, and there is no place He cannot see. The darkest corner of your life right now is the same.
Meditate: Is there something in my life that I keep telling myself I can “turn back from at any time,” when in fact I no longer have the strength to paddle?

Pray: Lord Jesus, You walked into death and came out of death again. I confess that I cannot paddle my way out by myself. Reach in from outside and take hold of me, and set my feet on a rock. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: Selflessness overcomes self-centeredness: a massive star spends its whole life holding itself up by shining outward, and when it stops giving out, it collapses inward. Life has a similar danger: when everything is drawn in toward the self, life contracts tighter and tighter.

Jesus is my example: He did not stand on the shore and shout; He went down to the very deepest place Himself. When we accompany someone stuck in a pit, we too must be willing to go down and sit beside him.
Let Jesus reign: bring out that matter you say “I can handle myself,” and ask a spiritual companion to keep watch for you.

blocks.h: This week: Write down one habit you have repeatedly tried and failed to give up, tell a trusted brother or sister, and ask them to check in with you once this week. If lately you feel your life has no way out, or you do not want to live any more, please talk to someone today. In Taiwan you can call the Peace of Mind Hotline 1925 or Lifeline 1995; elsewhere, please find your local crisis line. Being stuck in a pit does not necessarily mean you sinned. You deserve to be accompanied.
Pass it on: Is there something in your life that you felt you could turn back from at any time, and only later discovered you could not?
Quick quiz

quiz.q: According to general relativity, what happens when you cross the event horizon of a supermassive black hole?
o: You are torn apart on the spot
You would not feel anything special at that moment
quiz.e: The line itself carries no marker; tidal forces become deadly only farther in.

quiz.q: What is the current status of Hawking radiation?
o: A theoretical prediction, not yet directly observed
It has been proven not to exist
quiz.e: The Hawking temperature of a stellar-mass black hole is far below the cosmic background radiation, so the signal cannot be measured.

quiz.q: How does this unit view the relationship between black holes and spiritual truth?
o: A black hole is the hell the Bible speaks of
Science has proven the existence of sin
A black hole is only an analogy for meditation, and in itself a celestial object God made
quiz.e: An analogy can help meditation, but it is not a physical conclusion, and a black hole must not be equated with hell.

units.title: The Unseen Universe
units.sub: All the stars, the oceans, and you add up to only about 5% of the universe. For the rest, humanity still has no name.

share.v: By faith we understand that the universe has been framed by the word of God, so that what is seen has not been made out of things which are visible.

blocks.h: Every book you have ever read, every star you have ever seen, every bowl of braised pork rice you have ever eaten: the kind of matter they are made of makes up only about 5% of the universe.
The other 95%: scientists know only what it does, and cannot yet say what it is. The farther human telescopes see, the more clearly we realize how much we have not seen.
Behold, these are but the outskirts of his ways. How small a whisper do we hear of him! But the thunder of his power who can understand?”
The stars are spinning too fast

In the solar system, the farther a planet is from the Sun, the slower it moves: the Earth travels about 30 kilometers per second, while Neptune manages only a little over 5. In 1933 the Swiss astronomer Fritz Zwicky found that the galaxies in the Coma Cluster were moving too fast to be held together by the visible mass alone, and he called the missing material “dark matter.” His numbers were far off at the time, and the idea lay quiet for decades.

In the 1970s the American astronomers Vera Rubin and Kent Ford measured Andromeda and many spiral galaxies and found that the stars on the outskirts did not slow down as expected. To explain this flat curve, there has to be a large amount of unseen mass around the outside of the galaxy. In 1965 she had fought for the chance to observe at Palomar Observatory, becoming the first woman allowed to do so; there was no women’s restroom there, and she is said to have solved the problem by cutting a paper skirt and sticking it on the little figure on the men’s room door.

When you watch Taiwanese glove puppet theater, you cannot see the master’s hand; you see only the puppet doing somersaults and swinging a big sword. Yet no one thinks the puppet is flying about by itself: by how it moves, you know there is a hand behind the curtain. Astronomers reason about dark matter in the same way: when something visible moves in a way that is not right, they infer that something unseen is pulling. The difference is that dark matter is only a kind of matter, not a master with a will.

The word “dark” can also mislead. It does not mean black. It is more like a glass door that has been wiped too clean: light passes straight through, you cannot see it, and you only know it is there when you walk into it. The way dark matter “bumps into” us is gravity.
The Bullet Cluster: pulling matter and gravity apart

About 3.7 billion light-years away, the Bullet Cluster is the scene of two galaxy clusters colliding. Most of the ordinary matter in a cluster is hot gas, and in the collision the gas dragged against itself and stayed in the middle; yet the mass distribution mapped by gravitational lensing followed the galaxies out to the two sides. In 2006 Douglas Clowe and colleagues measured this offset at 8 standard deviations and presented it as strong evidence for the existence of dark matter.

items.h: About 27% of the universe is a kind of matter that does not interact with light. It can explain galaxy rotation, the Bullet Cluster, the cosmic microwave background and large-scale structure all at once, and it is the current mainstream view. Its weakness is that no dark matter particle has ever been directly detected.

In 1983 Mordehai Milgrom proposed that perhaps the law of gravity is different at extremely small accelerations. With very few parameters, this idea describes galaxy rotation curves beautifully. Its weakness is that at the scale of galaxy clusters there is still mass it cannot explain, and it has difficulty covering all cosmological observations at once.

blocks.h: Direct detection efforts continue. The LZ experiment, deep underground in South Dakota, waits for dark matter particles to strike about seven tonnes of liquid xenon; in 2025 it published 4.2 tonne-years of data. It saw no signal and only narrowed the possible range. Other candidates, such as axions, remain unconfirmed.
Dark energy: even the definition is still changing

In 1998 two teams found from distant supernovae that the universe is expanding at an accelerating rate. The component driving this is called dark energy, about 68% of the whole. The simplest model treats it as an unchanging cosmological constant. But the DESI survey, using more than 14 million galaxies and quasars, reported in 2025 that the data lean toward dark energy changing over time, with a significance of about 2.8 to 4.2 standard deviations depending on which supernova data are combined. That has not reached the 5 standard deviations physics customarily requires, and some studies suggest the lean may be affected by systematic errors in low-redshift supernova data. For now it is a clue worth following, not a conclusion.
“Unseen” is easily misused. Let us look at how to sort it into layers.

According to the Planck satellite’s 2018 fit of the standard model, the universe is made up of about 5% ordinary matter, 27% dark matter and 68% dark energy. These are measured values within that model.
The rotation speeds at the edges of galaxies are far higher than the visible mass can explain. This is a direct observational fact.
That these anomalies come from a real dark matter is the mainstream explanation, and the Bullet Cluster is strong evidence; modified gravity still has a minority of serious supporters.
Dark matter particles have still not been directly detected; whether dark energy changes over time is unsettled, with a lean of 2.8 to 4.2 standard deviations.

That most of the universe is unseen by humans undermines the intuition that “if I can’t see it, it doesn’t exist,” and it should make us humble. But it does not prove God, and dark matter must not be equated with the spiritual realm or angels; dark matter is created matter that we simply do not yet know.

Here is an honest objection to consider: someone may say that dark matter can be tested by experiment and God cannot, so the two cannot be compared. There is something to that, which is why we do not put God into the gaps in science. If dark matter is someday solved, faith loses nothing.
Unseen is one thing; without basis is another

The Bible very early divides the created order into the seen and the unseen, and attributes both to Christ. This passage is about all authority and created things, not about dark matter; but it teaches us not to measure reality with our eyes.

For by him all things were created in the heavens and on the earth, visible things and invisible things, whether thrones or dominions or principalities or powers. All things have been created through him and for him. He is before all things, and in him all things are held together.
By faith we understand that the universe has been framed by the word of God, so that what is seen has not been made out of things which are visible.
The unseen God came to where we can see

Astronomers can only infer dark matter from how the stars move. If God left us only this kind of clue, the most we could do is guess that “there may be a hand behind the curtain.” The Christian claim is bolder: the curtain has been pulled back, and the unseen God came personally to people. By the Sea of Galilee He grilled fish for His disciples, He bled on the cross, and on the third day He rose, so that people saw and touched Him.
He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.
No one has seen God at any time. The only born Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has declared him.

Tonight find a place to look up at the stars. All that you can see is only a small corner of the universe. Then look at your hand: it is made of that 5%, and it is remembered by the Lord who made the other 95%.
Meditate: Do I take seriously only what can be seen, such as achievements, savings and applause, and forget that the unseen things are what hold everything up?

Pray: Lord whom we cannot see, in Jesus You let us see You. I confess that what I know is only a whisper. Save me from the pride of thinking I understand it all, and open my eyes to care for what is eternal. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: Change your mindset: turn from the temporary and visible to the eternal. The prayer and service no one sees today are not zero with God.
Humility overcomes pride: if we do not even know what 95% of the universe is, we can say “I understand this” a little less often, letting God be God and people be people.
People matter more than things: what truly holds up a family or a church is often unseen forgiveness, watchfulness and faithfulness. Life first, then relationships, then ministry.

blocks.h: This week: Find one person who has quietly held you up from behind. Perhaps it is an elder who prays for you, or a coworker who is always tidying the venue. Write a few specific words to thank them.
Pass it on: Scientists say that about 95% of the universe is something we do not yet know. Do you feel there is something in life that is unseen, yet the most real?
Quick quiz

quiz.q: What did Rubin and her colleagues find when they measured spiral galaxies?
o: Stars on the outskirts moved faster than expected
There are no stars at the galaxy’s center
Galaxies do not rotate at all
quiz.e: The outskirts did not slow down as expected, which suggests a large amount of unseen mass.

quiz.q: Which statement about dark matter is most accurate today?
o: An experiment has caught dark matter particles
Dark matter is the spiritual realm the Bible speaks of
The gravitational evidence is strong, but the particles have not been directly detected
quiz.e: The evidence comes from gravitational effects; LZ and other experiments have seen no signal so far, and it must not be equated with the spiritual realm.

quiz.q: How should we understand DESI’s 2025 result on dark energy?
o: It confirmed that dark energy changes
It is a clue worth following, not yet a conclusion
It proved that dark energy does not exist
quiz.e: The significance is 2.8 to 4.2 standard deviations, short of the customary 5, and systematic errors are under discussion.

units.title: Exoplanets: Are We Alone?
units.sub: Humanity has been calling out to the stars for more than sixty years and has heard no reply. Someone began calling to us long before that.

share.v: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.”

blocks.h: On November 16, 1974, the Arecibo telescope in Puerto Rico sent a message toward M13, a star cluster in the constellation Hercules. It was 1,679 bits long and took less than three minutes. The address was 25,000 light-years away. Even if someone wrote back at once, the reply would take about 50,000 years to arrive.
This may be the most patient text message humanity has ever sent. It voices a very old question in our hearts: is anyone out there?
When I consider your heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars, which you have ordained, what is man, that you think of him? What is the son of man, that you care for him?
From none at all to more than six thousand

In 1992 Wolszczan and Frail found planets around a pulsar. In 1995 Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz of the Geneva Observatory announced the first exoplanet orbiting a Sun-like star: 51 Pegasi b, a giant planet that completes an orbit in about four days. No solar system textbook at the time had anything like it. The two received the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physics. Today NASA’s Exoplanet Archive lists 6,451 confirmed planets (consulted November 2026), of which 2,787 were found by the Kepler Space Telescope, which operated from 2009 to 2018.

Exoplanets are too faint to see directly, so astronomers work like detectives. Imagine seeing someone far off walking at night, being tugged along by a black dog. You cannot see the dog, but you can see the owner swaying. This is the radial velocity method: Jupiter makes the Sun wobble at about 13 meters per second, and the Earth only about 9 centimeters per second. Another method is like staring at a street lamp and waiting for a firefly to fly across it: when an Earth-sized planet passes in front of a Sun-like star, it dims the star by only about eight parts in a hundred thousand.
How are the closest candidates doing?

TRAPPIST-1 is about 40 light-years away and has seven Earth-sized rocky planets. The James Webb Space Telescope measured the innermost, TRAPPIST-1b, and the results show it has no obvious thick atmosphere. What about TRAPPIST-1e, in the habitable zone? Preliminary 2025 observations ruled out only some cases. It may be bare rock, or it may have a nitrogen-containing atmosphere; it is not yet certain, and the main obstacle is that the host star is too active.

K2-18b has made many headlines. In 2025 Nikku Madhusudhan’s team reported a 3-standard-deviation hint of dimethyl sulfide from Webb data, a molecule that on Earth comes mainly from living things. The same year Renyu Hu and colleagues (Madhusudhan is also among the authors) analyzed more transits and found that none of the related signals exceeded 3 standard deviations, and pointed out that non-biological chemistry could also produce these molecules. Conclusion: unconfirmed. Whenever a headline says “alien life discovered,” read the body text first.
Fermi’s lunch question

In the summer of 1950 the physicist Enrico Fermi was walking to lunch with colleagues at Los Alamos when he asked, in effect: so where is everybody? The exact words are remembered differently by those present. If the Milky Way has so many planets, civilizations should have spread everywhere long ago, so why is there not a single trace? In 1961 Frank Drake proposed his famous equation, which he himself treated as an agenda for discussion and not a calculator; the later factors are still unknown to anyone.

items.h: Planets and organic molecules are common, and the Milky Way has hundreds of billions of stars. We have been searching seriously for only about sixty years, and the range we have searched is still small. Not hearing a signal does not mean there is none.

In 2000 Ward and Brownlee proposed the “Rare Earth” hypothesis: complex life needs a long chain of lucky conditions. Critics say the conditions they chose are too tailored to Earth, and many of those conditions have been questioned.

In 2018 Sandberg and colleagues pointed out that once the huge uncertainties in each factor are included, the chance that we are the only intelligent life in the observable universe is actually not small, and so it is not surprising.

blocks.h: One analysis of Kepler data once estimated that about 22% of Sun-like stars have an Earth-sized planet in the habitable zone. Follow-up studies give quite different numbers, and the habitable zone only means that liquid water could possibly exist, which is a long way from “there is life.”
This topic is especially prone to two kinds of exaggeration: “there must be aliens” and “there absolutely are no aliens.”
Exoplanets are common, with more than 6,400 confirmed (2026).
How common Earth-like planets are is still very uncertain, with widely differing estimates.
No life beyond Earth has been confirmed so far. The dimethyl sulfide signal at K2-18b has not reached the standard for confirmation, and a non-biological source is possible.
The answer to the Fermi paradox is unsettled: rare Earth, short-lived civilizations, not having searched long enough, and the paradox itself being flawed each have supporters.
The Bible does not say explicitly whether there is life beyond Earth. Christians can hold different views without affecting the core of the faith; the center of the gospel is God seeking people.
Perspectives Room
What if extraterrestrial life were really discovered one day? There is no single answer among Christians.

items.h: The Bible’s story of salvation is centered on Earth, and Christ became human as a descendant of Adam. This camp tends to think the human situation is unique. To stay humble: this is an inference, and the Bible does not say it directly.

items.n: Microbes are no problem; intelligent life is another matter
items.h: If it were only microbes, almost no doctrine would be affected, and the Bible also speaks of God caring for living things other than humans. If they were created beings with moral awareness, there would be hard questions to think through, such as whether they had fallen and whether they would need redemption.

God’s creation is not limited by our imagination. As early as the 15th century the theologian William Vorilong discussed the possibility of Christ redeeming other worlds, and in our day the Methodist scholar David Wilkinson has written a book on it. The “once” of Hebrews 9:26 is a text that must be taken seriously.

blocks.h: The first question in human history

Humans have long asked, “Is anyone out there?” But the Bible records a question going in the other direction: after people sinned and hid among the trees, God spoke first. The almighty God does not lack information. He asked so that the one in hiding would know that someone was looking for him.
Yahweh God called to the man, and said to him, “Where are you?”

Humans search the stars for a signal; God was already calling at our hiding place. Loneliness is real: the World Health Organization estimated in 2025 that about one in six people worldwide suffers from it. But the Bible says that the source of our deepest loneliness is separation from God.
“Which of you men, if you had one hundred sheep and lost one of them, wouldn’t leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that was lost, until he found it?
For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.”
How far did He go to seek? All the way to the cross. There Jesus cried out the loneliest sentence ever spoken, so that all who trust Him would never have to walk the darkest road alone.
“Eli, Eli, lima sabachthani?” That is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off are made near in the blood of Christ.

Tonight look at any one star in the sky and tell yourself: there is very likely a planet beside that star, and I do not know what is there. Then look with the same gaze at the person near you who has lately been speaking less.
Meditate: Where am I hiding? When God asks me today, “Where are you?”, what can I honestly answer?

Pray: Lord who seeks me, humanity waits for an echo from the stars, yet You came first and called me. Thank You for going to the cross to seek me, the lost one. Make me also an echo to others in their loneliness. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: Jesus is my example: He took the initiative to seek people. I will not wait for others to care for me; I will go first to look for the one lost sheep.

People matter more than tasks: we are willing to spend decades and build antennas hundreds of meters wide to wait for one signal; the person beside you may need only ten minutes with your phone put down.
920 relationships: treat every relationship as a lesson the Lord has given me, set myself aside, and let the fruit of the Spirit grow where the other person can taste it.

blocks.h: This week: Contact a friend you have not been in touch with for more than three months. No forwarding, no selling, just ask “How have you been lately?” and then listen to the whole answer.
Pass it on: If one day it were really confirmed that there is other life in the universe, would that make humanity more alone, or less alone?
Quick quiz

quiz.q: What is the current status of dimethyl sulfide at K2-18b?
o: The signal has not reached the standard for confirmation, and a non-biological source is possible
It has been completely ruled out
quiz.e: There are hints, there is dispute, and it is unconfirmed; it cannot be said to be completely ruled out either.

quiz.q: How should the Drake equation be understood?
o: Drake used it to calculate the exact number of civilizations
It has been proven that there are no other civilizations in the Milky Way
It is an agenda for organizing discussion, and its later factors are still unknown
quiz.e: Drake himself used it as an agenda for discussion, not to arrive at a definite answer.

quiz.q: What is this unit’s position on extraterrestrial life?
o: The Bible does not say explicitly, Christians hold different views, and the center of the gospel is God seeking people
quiz.e: This is a peripheral question where different views can sit side by side; the core is Christ’s salvation.

units.title: Time and Eternity
units.sub: Your head is actually a tiny bit older than your feet. Time stretches and shrinks, and the eternal God walked into time.

share.v: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in their hearts, yet so that man can’t find out the work that God has done from the beginning even to the end.

blocks.h: Right now your head is a tiny bit older than your feet. The difference is so small that you could never feel it in a lifetime, yet someone has already measured it.

In 2022 American scientists measured, within a single cloud of atoms, two layers about 1 millimeter apart, one above the other, in which time ran at different speeds. Time, it turns out, is not one big clock on the wall shared by the whole universe.
He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in their hearts, yet so that man can’t find out the work that God has done from the beginning even to the end.
Time stretches and shrinks

Einstein’s relativity makes two predictions: the faster something moves, the slower its clock runs; and the weaker the gravity (the farther from Earth), the faster the clock runs. In October 1971 Hafele and Keating flew cesium atomic clocks around the world on commercial airliners. The clocks flown eastward ran about 59 nanoseconds slow compared with the ground, and the clocks flown westward ran about 273 nanoseconds fast, in rough agreement with the predictions.

Your phone’s navigation uses this every day. GPS satellites move fast, so their clocks lose about 7 microseconds a day; but the satellites are high up, where gravity is weaker, so their clocks gain about 45 microseconds a day. Added together, the net gain is about 38 microseconds a day. If engineers did not correct for it, the positioning error between two clock synchronizations could build up to about 11 kilometers.

Think of time as a river whose width stays the same but whose current is not the same everywhere. You and a friend each take a boat and set your watches together at the start, then follow different channels. When you meet again, the two watches no longer agree. Neither watch is broken; the two of you really did experience different amounts of time.
Why does time only move forward?

A broken cup does not put itself back together, and a fried egg cannot go back into its shell. Physics describes this direction with “entropy”: the disorder of a closed system tends to increase. The strange thing is that the basic equations describing microscopic collisions hardly distinguish forward from backward. So where does the direction come from?

The mainstream view is called the “Past Hypothesis”: the universe began in a state of extremely low entropy and has moved toward high entropy ever since. The idea can be traced back to Boltzmann, and the name comes from the philosopher David Albert. Roger Penrose estimated that such an initial state is only about 1 in 1010123 of all possible states. Why it is so remains unsettled, and some scholars have proposed models that do not need this hypothesis.

To be honest, physics has not finished answering “what exactly is time?” The definition of the second is certainly precise: the duration of 9,192,631,770 oscillations of the radiation from a certain energy transition in the cesium-133 atom. But that only tells us how to measure it. About 1,600 years ago, what Augustine wrote in Book 11 of the Confessions still holds today. His gist was this: if no one asks me, I know what time is; if someone asks and I want to explain it, I do not know.

Precision keeps improving. In 2010 optical clocks at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) measured the time difference caused by a height difference of 33 centimeters and a speed difference of about 10 meters per second. The 2022 experiment shrank the height difference to about 1 millimeter, with a frequency difference of about 10−19. And in 1977 a storage-ring experiment at CERN found that muons circling at nearly the speed of light lived about 64.4 microseconds, stretched from about 2.2 microseconds at rest.
Let us separate physical fact, scholarly discussion and inference of faith.
Time dilation has been confirmed by many kinds of experiments, including atomic clocks on airplanes, muons in storage rings and optical clocks.
The net relativistic effect on GPS satellite clocks is about 38 microseconds fast per day, and the system was designed with this already accounted for.
The arrow of time is connected to the low-entropy state at the beginning of the universe; this is the mainstream view, but whether and how that low-entropy state can be explained is still debated.
In the Bible, “a thousand years as one day” speaks of God’s patience and transcendence, not of a foretelling of relativity. To take it as “the Bible knew relativity all along” is over-interpretation.
A God who transcends time and also enters time can answer the longing for eternity in the human heart. This is a theological claim; physics neither confirms nor denies it.
Perspectives Room
What is God’s relationship to time? Even among evangelicals there are different views. They are set side by side below, without a ruling.

items.h: The tradition running from Augustine through Boethius to Aquinas: God has no before and after, no past and future; Boethius described it as possessing unending life all at once and completely. Its strength is that it best protects God’s completeness and unchangeableness; its difficulty is how such a God responds to a prayer at a particular moment.

Nicholas Wolterstorff and others hold that God has no beginning and no end, but experiences before and after. The Bible often describes God responding, waiting and changing His course of action, and this view stays close to the biblical narrative; its difficulty is how to account for God’s omniscience and unchangeableness.

William Lane Craig holds that without creation God is timeless, and that after creation God enters a temporal relationship with the world. Critics think the transition itself is hard to explain clearly.

blocks.h: He is not chased by time
We all live in a countdown. God does not. Moses’ prayer sets our brevity beside God’s eternity.

Before the mountains were born, before you had formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, you are God. For a thousand years in your sight are just like yesterday when it is past, like a watch in the night.
Peter uses the same words to answer an anxious question: why has the Lord’s promised coming not happened yet? His answer is not a conversion formula. It is the heart of God.
The Lord is not slow concerning his promise, as some count slowness; but he is patient with us, not wishing that anyone should perish, but that all should come to repentance.
Eternity walked into the calendar
Here is the most astonishing part: this God who is not limited by time chose an era, a place and a mother. He got hungry, He got tired, and He died on a Friday.
But when the fullness of the time came, God sent out his Son, born to a woman, born under the law, that he might redeem those who were under the law, that we might receive the adoption as children.

The cross was an event on one particular day in history, but its effect reaches past that day. The resurrection on the third day turned “eternal life” from a longing into a promise one can lean on. And Jesus’ definition of eternal life is first of all a relationship.
This is eternal life, that they should know you, the only true God, and him whom you sent, Jesus Christ.

Turn on your phone’s location and look at that blue dot. Think: it is accurate because someone took seriously a difference in time that you cannot feel. Then put the phone down, be quiet for one minute and do nothing, and hand that minute directly to the eternal Lord.
Meditate: About which matter do I most often tell God, “It’s too late”? If He is not in a hurry, yet cares about me very much, how would that matter look different?

Pray: God from everlasting to everlasting, my days are short, and I am often anxious and often full of regret. Thank You for sending the Lord Jesus into my history when the fullness of time came. Teach me to count my days, and I place my regrets about the past and my worries about the future into Your hands. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: Turn from a temporary viewpoint to an eternal one: with the same schedule, ask, “Ten years from now, in eternity, will this still matter?”
People matter more than tasks: time is given for relationships. Keep the best part of your time for people, and not only for the to-do list.
Letting God be God: His timetable is not mine to manage. Drop the habit of pressing God, and concentrate on doing what is to be done today.

blocks.h: This week: Pick one day, put your phone in a drawer for 30 minutes, and give your full attention to one person, or pray in quiet. At the end write down one sentence: what I saw in those 30 minutes.
Pass it on: If you could go back and say one sentence to your past self, what would it be? Why do you think people always want something longer than this one life?
Quick quiz

quiz.q: What is the net relativistic effect on GPS satellite clocks, roughly?
quiz.e: The speed effect makes them about 7 microseconds slow and the gravity effect about 45 microseconds fast, for a net of about 38 microseconds fast.

quiz.q: In context, what is “a thousand years as one day” in 2 Peter 3:8 mainly about?
o: The Lord’s promise is not slow; He is being patient with people
A conversion formula in which one day equals a thousand years
quiz.e: Verse 9 goes on to explain: the Lord is not slow but patient, wishing that all should come to repentance.
